newsitem.title: MALI: Main opposition to boycott July 20 Mali poll rerun.
newsitem.headline: Main opposition to boycott July 20 Mali poll rerun.

text.p: Almost 600 candidates will stand for Mali's 147 national assembly seats on July 20 in a rerun parliamentary election but the main opposition will boycott the poll, the constitutional court announced.

The court, which scrapped an April poll citing organisational chaos, said candidates cleared to run included members of President Alpha Oumar Konare's Alliance for Democracy in Mali (ADEMA), 18 other parties and 13 independent lists.
Mali was widely praised for its 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship to a multi-party system.
Konare pressed ahead with a May 11 presidential election, won the backing of the court for that and then the election.

The main opposition parties -- the National Congress for Democratic Initiative (CNID), the Rally for Democracy and Progress (RDP), the Patriotic Movement for Renewal (MPR) and the Union of Democratic and Popular Forces (UFDP) -- had demanded that the whole election process be reviewed and reorganised.
They boycotted the presidential election. Konare won with 84.36 percent of votes in the first round.
ADEMA will contest all 55 of the former French colony's constituencies in July. The second round is on August 6.

The Party for Unity, Democracy and Progress (PUDP) of Mamadou Maribatrou Diaby, who defied the opposition boycott to stand against Konare, will contest 35 constituencies. The other 17 parties will each contest fewer constituencies.
The constitutional court ruled numerous irregularities had flawed the scrapped April 13 first round parliamentary vote.
